description: This bar chart, titled “Researcher Location,” illustrates the number of datasets associated with different researcher locations over time, from 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the year, with labels for each year from 2012 to 2022. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each bar corresponds to a specific year and is composed of multiple colored segments representing different researcher locations, as indicated in the legend: blue for “Other,” red for “UK,” orange for “USA,” purple for “IT,” green for “IN,” and brown for “DE.” The bars are not grouped but are stacked vertically within each year, with each color segment representing the contribution of that location to the total number of datasets for that year. The chart shows that the total number of datasets generally increases over time, with the most significant growth occurring between 2016 and 2021. In 2022, the “Other” category (blue) shows the highest number of datasets, followed by “USA” (orange) and “IN” (green). The “UK” (red) and “IT” (purple) categories show relatively low values in most years, with “IT” showing a slight increase in 2022. The “DE” (brown) category is consistently low, with only one bar visible in 2015 and a small segment in 2022. The chart does not indicate any specific sorting order for the bars, and no bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or annotations.
